-   **Rarity note:** Migratory bird found throughout Florida in wooded wetlands, hammocks, cypress swamps, bottomland forests, and mangroves.

## Natural history notes

A small migratory warbler characterized by bluish-gray upperparts, yellow throat and breast, white eye arcs, and a greenish back patch, with males often showing a darker chest band. In Florida, it is found in wooded wetlands, hammocks, cypress swamps, bottomland forests, mangroves, and mature forests with Spanish moss or other epiphytes used for nesting. It feeds mainly on insects, spiders, and other small arthropods, foraging actively among leaves, branches, and hanging vegetation in the midstory and canopy.
